identity.description:
D8 measure, phase 2: history and tests stay at one pass, with the by-pass report (0.13.0)

D8 "measure", phase 2: the passes measurement, its note, and the by-pass report that made it. Version 0.13.0.

## Result

history and tests stay at one pass. The defaults do not change, so the README worst case and the design stay as they are, and no gate run was needed.

One repeat of history and tests at two passes, on the 28 pinned cases, cost $89.15 of the $150 budget. The two passes of one reviewer are two independent samples of one pass, so each reviewer gives three sets: pass 1, pass 2 and both.

| Reviewer | Goldens pass 1 / pass 2 / both | R (90% interval) | Precision one pass → both | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| history | 22 / 22 / 26 | 4.83 (2.68 to 10.18) | 0.880 → 0.839 | (b) fails, (c) holds: one pass |
| tests | 27 / 27 / 28 | 19.29 (7.70 to unbounded) | 0.593 → 0.483 | (b) and (c) fail: one pass |

R is the added cost per added posted-label golden over the one-pass cost per golden. The rule: two passes when the upper end of the interval of R is at most 2 and the precision of both is no more than 0.05 below the one-pass precision. `docs/research/passes-recall.md` holds every figure, the definitions, the seed and the count of resamples.

The run records of the D4b baseline do not exist, so there are no figures for diff-bugs and security.

## Code

- `pr-review eval-report --by-pass` scores the pass 1, pass 2 and both sets per reviewer and for all multi-pass reviewers together, from the stored records and judge answers, with no model call. It prints the one-pass mean, the noise of one pass, the added goldens, false findings and cost, a seeded percentile bootstrap (seed 20261114, 10000 resamples, 90%) and the decision tests (b) and (c).
- `--ask-missing` asks only the judge questions that a single-pass set needs and that the live run never asked, and stores the answers in the judge cache. The measurement used it for 2 questions ($0.02).
- New modules: `src/eval/by-pass.ts`, `src/eval/bootstrap.ts`. 18 tests in `test/eval-by-pass.test.ts`.

## TICKETS.md

The D8 entry now states what was done: no subset (one repeat of all 28 cases fit the budget), the three-set report, the new decision rule and why it replaces the first one, and the result.

## Decisions

- The principal chose one repeat of all 28 cases over three repeats of a ten-case subset, because the count of goldens decides how stable the result is.
- The principal replaced the rule "gain above zero in every repeat" (it cannot fail in a paired design) with tests (b) and (c), before the figures existed.
- Definitions accepted by the principal: the one-pass precision is pooled over the two single sets; the one-pass cost per golden is the mean single-set cost over the mean single-set goldens. Run-wide queries (triage, merge) are in no set's cost.

## Checks

`npm test` (1495 tests), `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` pass. The new tests fail at the red commit 4af4d3f.

triage.summary: Adds `pr-review eval-report --by-pass`, which scores pass 1, pass 2 and both for each reviewer with two passes. It reports a bootstrap interval and applies a cost-ratio and precision decision rule. `--ask-missing` lets the judge answer uncached questions and writes them to the judge cache. It also adds docs, a research note on the history and tests measurement, and a version bump to 0.13.0.
